title: Protocols for SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Primary Ocular Cells and Eye Organoids
author: Eriksen, Møller, et al.

steps.title: Passage cells to feeder‑free
steps.instruction: If stem cells are grown on feeder layers, passage them into feeder‑free conditions for at least two passages before initiating SEAM differentiation.

steps.title: Coat plates with Synthemax‑II‑SC
steps.instruction: Coat four wells of a 24‑well plate per donor tissue type with Synthemax‑II‑SC according to the manufacturer’s guidelines.

steps.title: Prepare collagenase solution
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL centrifuge tube (one per tissue type except RPE), add 3 mL of 2.5 mg/mL collagenase II, 0.6 µL thiazovivin (final 40 nM), and 9 µL DNase I (1 U/µL); heat to 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare trypsin‑EDTA solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 5 mL trypsin‑EDTA containing 40 nM thiazovivin and 3 µL/mL DNase I; heat to 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare warm TAB2 media
steps.instruction: Prepare 30 mL TAB2 medium supplemented with an additional 10 % hi‑FBS and 40 nM thiazovivin; heat to 37 °C.

steps.title: Sterilize whole globe (if received)
steps.instruction: Submerge the whole globe in 30 % betadine solution, rinse twice with sterile PBS, then proceed to dissection. If only a cornea rejected for transplant is received, skip this sterilization step.

steps.title: Isolate sclera, cornea, limbus
steps.instruction: Dissect, digest, and plate scleral, corneal, and limbal tissues.

substeps.instruction: a. Make a circular cut separating sclera from limbus and cornea; place sclera in a petri dish with sterile PBS.
b. Make a circular cut separating limbus from cornea; place limbus and cornea in separate petri dishes with sterile PBS.
c. Aspirate PBS from each dish.
d. Cut each tissue into ~1 mm² pieces with a scalpel or scissors.
e. Transfer tissue pieces to the prepared collagenase‑II tube; loosely close the lid for gas exchange and incubate at 37 °C for 2 h, triturating with a P1000 pipette after 1 h.
f. Add 300 µL hi‑FBS to the tube and triturate to mix.
g. Pellet cells by centrifugation at 300 × g for 5 min.
h. Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells in 2 mL TAB2 medium containing 10 % FBS and 40 nM thiazovivin.
i. Divide the suspension into four Synthemax‑II‑SC‑coated 24‑well wells (500 µL per well) and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 20 % O₂.

steps.title: Isolate iris and ciliary marginal zone
steps.instruction: Dissect iris and ciliary marginal zone, digest, and plate as for other tissues.

substeps.instruction: a. Cut the ciliary marginal zone from the choroid at the top of the globe and transfer iris plus ciliary marginal zone to a petri dish with sterile PBS.
b. Separate iris from the ciliary marginal zone using angled tweezers for iris and blunt tweezers for the marginal zone.
c. Place the isolated iris in a clean petri dish.
d. Cut iris into small pieces with a scalpel or scissors.
e. Transfer pieces to a collagenase‑II tube; loosely close lid and incubate at 37 °C for 2 h, triturating after 1 h.
f. Add 300 µL hi‑FBS and triturate.
g. Pellet cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
h. Aspirate supernatant and resuspend in 2 mL TAB2 medium with 10 % FBS and 40 nM thiazovivin.
i. Plate 500 µL per well into four Synthemax‑II‑SC‑coated 24‑well wells and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 20 % O₂.

steps.title: Isolate retinal pigment epithelium
steps.instruction: Detach RPE cells from the choroid, inactivate trypsin, and plate.

substeps.instruction: a. Fix the choroid to the sclera by inserting 3–4 equally spaced 27‑gauge needles around the globe opening.
b. Lift out the lens and vitreous; if the retina is not attached, carefully detach it from the pigmented layer and discard.
c. Add ~3 mL warm trypsin containing 40 nM thiazovivin and 3 µL/mL DNase I to the globe, filling to ~1 mm below the choroid‑RPE rim.
d. Incubate the globe for 45 min at 37 °C.
e. Gently agitate with a sterilized brush to detach RPE cells; the trypsin solution will become pigmented.
f. Transfer the cell suspension to a centrifuge tube and add 1/10 total volume (~300 µL) hi‑FBS to inactivate trypsin.
g. Pellet cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
h. Aspirate supernatant and resuspend in 2 mL TAB2 medium with 10 % FBS and 40 nM thiazovivin.
i. Plate 500 µL per well into four Synthemax‑II‑SC‑coated 24‑well wells and incubate at 37 °C (CO₂/O₂ conditions as above).

steps.title: Isolate choroid
steps.instruction: Digest choroid tissue, pellet, and plate cells.

substeps.instruction: a. Gently wash the choroid with sterile PBS to reduce RPE contamination.
b. Peel the choroid from the globe using blunt tweezers and place in a clean petri dish.
c. Cut the tissue into small pieces with a scalpel or scissors.
d. Transfer pieces to a collagenase‑II tube; loosely close lid and incubate at 37 °C for 2 h, triturating after 1 h.
e. Add 300 µL hi‑FBS and triturate.
f. Pellet cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
g. Aspirate supernatant and resuspend in 2 mL TAB2 medium with 10 % FBS and 40 nM thiazovivin.
h. Plate 500 µL per well into four Synthemax‑II‑SC‑coated 24‑well wells and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 20 % O₂.

steps.title: Initial adhesion and media maintenance
steps.instruction: Allow all newly plated ocular cells to adhere for at least 48 h without disturbance; thereafter replace media with fresh TAB2 every 2–4 days. Optional: add 10 % hi‑FBS to boost proliferation; once confluent, reduce FBS to 2–5 %.

steps.title: Expand cultured ocular cells
steps.instruction: Passage cells when confluent using trypsin, then re‑plate at a 1:4 ratio.

substeps.instruction: a. Aspirate media and wash cells once with Ca²⁺‑ and Mg²⁺‑free PBS.
b. Add 0.5 mL trypsin to each well and incubate until cells round up and detach.
c. Inactivate trypsin by adding 0.5 mL 10 % hi‑FBS in PBS to each well.
d. Gently agitate the plate, collect the cell suspension, and transfer to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
e. Pellet cells at 300 × g for 5 min.
f. Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells in TAB2 medium containing 10 % hi‑FBS and 40 nM thiazovivin; re‑plate at a 1:4 dilution onto fresh Synthemax‑II‑SC‑coated plates.
g. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 20 % O₂.

description: The protocol below describes how to grow self-formed ectodermal autonomous multizone (SEAM) eye organoids, modified from the original protocol published by Hayashi et al. (Hayashi et al., 2016). Here we describe the differentiation of human embryonic stem cell line H9 into SEAM, used to study infection with SARS-CoV-2 in the eye, as first presented by Eriksen et al. (Eriksen et al., 2021). However, we have also successfully differentiated induced pluripotent stem cell knockout lines and a dCas9-KRAB edited stem cell line using this methodology. If the stem cells are grown on feeder cells, passage the cells into feeder-free conditions for at least two passages prior to initiating SEAM differentiation. For the adult human cells, cells are freshly isolated from post-mortem donor globes or from cornea donor shells rejected for use as transplants. Tissue should be isolated in preservation solution within 12 h of death and processed for cell culture within 40 h. Shorter time intervals between tissue isolation and processing will result in a higher yield of viable cells. Before obtaining human tissue, make sure your lab follows the institutional guidelines on how to handle and dispose of biohazardous materials and that consent forms from the donor or donor’s family are in place. Before beginning work with infectious agents such as SARS-CoV-2, be sure the required licenses and safety protocols are in place for your lab. Beware that, different countries and institutions have different guidelines on how to work with infectious agents.
